units.explain: Pair of method-adapting decorators bridging deprecated pre-3.2 signatures (no AppContext first parameter) with the new ones on Flask. remove_ctx wraps an overriding method that still accepts ctx: if the first positional argument is an AppContext it is dropped before calling the wrapped function. add_ctx wraps the Flask base method: when invoked without arguments it prepends the current app context (app_ctx._get_current_object()); if the first argument is not an AppContext it is prepended so a super() call made with old-style args still receives the ctx. Both use functools.update_wrapper so the wrapper preserves metadata. Applied automatically by Flask.__init_subclass__ when a deprecated override is detected.
units.summary: Adapters that add or remove an AppContext first argument for deprecated method overrides.

relations.basis: wrappers typed for self: Flask and applied to Flask methods

uncertainties: Behavior when add_ctx runs with no active app context is not proven here

units.explain: Normalizes an optional value into a timedelta. None passes through as None, an existing timedelta is returned unchanged, and an int is interpreted as seconds and converted via timedelta(seconds=value). Pure function, no side effects.
units.summary: Convert an int (seconds) or None into a timedelta, passing timedelta through.

units.explain: Concrete WSGI application class subclassing the sansio App. The class body carries class-level state: the default_config mapping with all configuration keys (DEBUG, TESTING, PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS, SECRET_KEY, session cookie settings, SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT, TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS, PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS, etc.), request_class defaulted to flask.Request, response_class to flask.Response, and a class-wide session_interface instance of SecureCookieSessionInterface shared across instances. Its methods are documented as separate units; the residual module region between the class docstring region boundaries holds no executable symbols beyond these attributes.
units.summary: Concrete Flask WSGI app class holding default config, request/response classes, and session interface.

relations.basis: Flask(App) subclass declaration; base methods like add_url_rule are inherited

uncertainties: Behavior of inherited sansio App members is defined in flask/sansio/app.py, outside this batch

units.explain: Hook invoked when Flask is subclassed. It inspects a fixed list of lifecycle methods (handle_http_exception, handle_user_exception, handle_exception, log_exception, dispatch_request, full_dispatch_request, finalize_request, make_default_options_response, preprocess_request, process_response, do_teardown_request, do_teardown_appcontext). For each it compares the subclass attribute against the base Flask method; unoverridden methods are skipped. For overrides it reads the second parameter (first after self) and accepts it only if unannotated and named 'ctx', a string annotation ending in 'AppContext', or a class subclassing AppContext. Any other shape triggers a DeprecationWarning (old signature unsupported in Flask 4.0), then rebinds the subclass method through remove_ctx and sets the Flask base method to add_ctx(base_method) so old- and new-style callers interoperate. Side effect: mutates both the subclass and the Flask class attributes.
units.summary: Warns and adapts subclass overrides of lifecycle methods lacking the new ctx: AppContext parameter.
uncertainties: Whether repeated subclassing stacks add_ctx wrappers on the base method is not proven from this listing

extras.note: Sets attributes on both the subclass and the Flask base class when a deprecated override is found.

units.explain: Constructor forwards all parameters (import_name, static_url_path, static_folder, static_host, host_matching, subdomain_matching, template_folder, instance_path, instance_relative_config, root_path) to the sansio App constructor, then performs Flask-specific setup: creates self.cli as a cli.AppGroup named after the app, and if the app has a static folder registers the static route f'{static_url_path}/<path:filename>' with endpoint 'static'. Registration asserts static_host is given exactly when host_matching is True; the view is a lambda closing over a weakref to the app (avoiding a reference cycle) calling send_static_file. The static route is added without checking that the static folder exists.
units.summary: Initialize the app via the sansio base, add the CLI group, and register the static-files route.

relations.basis: self.add_url_rule(...) resolves to the inherited sansio method

extras.note: AssertionError if static_host and host_matching are inconsistent.

units.explain: Returns the cache max-age used when serving a file. Reads SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT from config: None returns None (conditional requests instead of a timed cache), a timedelta is converted to whole seconds as int, any other value is returned as-is. Pure lookup, no I/O.
units.summary: Resolve SEND_FILE_MAX_AGE_DEFAULT config into an int max-age or None.

units.explain: View function for the automatic static route. Raises RuntimeError if the app has no static folder. Otherwise computes max_age via get_send_file_max_age and delegates to helpers.send_from_directory with the static folder and filename, returning the resulting Response.
units.summary: Serve a file from the static folder via send_from_directory.

extras.note: RuntimeError when static_folder is not configured.

units.explain: Opens a file relative to root_path. Only read modes 'r', 'rt', 'rb' are allowed; anything else raises ValueError before any file access. Binary mode opens without an encoding; text mode passes the encoding argument (None means platform default). Returns the open file object with builtin open semantics (errors from open propagate).
units.summary: Open a read-only file relative to root_path, rejecting write modes.

units.explain: Opens a file relative to instance_path. Unlike open_resource, write modes are allowed: any mode containing 'b' opens in binary without encoding; other modes open in text with the given encoding (default 'utf-8'). Standard open errors propagate.
units.summary: Open a file relative to instance_path, allowing any mode including writing.

units.explain: Builds the Jinja Environment from a copy of jinja_options. If 'autoescape' is absent it defaults to select_jinja_autoescape; if 'auto_reload' is absent it uses TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD, falling back to self.debug when that config is None. Instantiates jinja_environment with self and the options, then injects globals: url_for, get_flashed_messages, config, and the request/session/g proxies (so imported templates can access them), and sets the json.dumps_function policy to self.json.dumps. Changing jinja_options after this call has no effect. Returns the Environment.
units.summary: Create the Jinja environment with Flask globals, autoescape, and auto_reload defaults.

units.explain: Creates the routing MapAdapter. With a request: assigns TRUSTED_HOSTS to request.trusted_hosts if configured, sets request.host from get_host over the environ and trusted hosts, then binds to the request environ. If url_map.host_matching is set, SERVER_NAME is deliberately omitted so the actual host is used; otherwise if subdomain_matching is off, the subdomain is forced to url_map.default_subdomain or '' to disable subdomain matching. Without a request, returns a server-bound adapter only if SERVER_NAME is configured (using APPLICATION_ROOT as script name and PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME as scheme); otherwise returns None.
units.summary: Bind the URL map to a request environ, or to SERVER_NAME when outside a request.
uncertainties: Exact bind_to_environ behavior for mismatched hosts is Werkzeug behavior not shown here

extras.note: Mutates request.trusted_hosts and request.host on the passed request.

units.explain: Re-raises the request's routing_exception to propagate it. In debug mode, when the exception is a RequestRedirect whose code is not 307/308 and the request method is not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (i.e. the redirect would discard the request body), it instead raises FormDataRoutingRedirect to give a clearer error. In all other cases (including non-debug) it raises the routing_exception itself, which may be None per the type-ignore comment — raising None would be a TypeError in Python; the code assumes a routing exception is present when called.
units.summary: Propagate routing exceptions, substituting a clearer error in debug for body-discarding redirects.
uncertainties: Behavior when routing_exception is None is not proven from the listing

units.explain: Mutates the given context dict in place with injected template variables. The name list starts with None (app-level processors) and, when the context has a request, extends with the request's blueprints reversed (most specific first). For each name with registered template_context_processors, each processor is run through ensure_sync and its dict result updates the context. Finally the original context values are re-applied on top, so explicit render_template values always win over processor-injected values and original keys are never overridden.
units.summary: Merge context-processor values into a template context, with caller values taking precedence.

units.explain: Builds the interactive shell namespace: starts with {'app': self, 'g': g} and updates it with the result of each registered shell_context_processor. Returns the resulting dict.
units.summary: Assemble the shell context from app, g, and shell context processors.

units.explain: Starts the local development server via werkzeug run_simple; not for production. If FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI is 'true', prints a red warning (unless running from the reloader) and returns without starting a server. If load_dotenv resolves true, cli.load_dotenv() runs and FLASK_DEBUG in the environment overrides the debug flag; an explicit debug argument overrides all sources afterwards. Host defaults to the host in SERVER_NAME, else '127.0.0.1'; port: explicit port (including 0) is coerced to int, else SERVER_NAME's port, else 5000. use_reloader and use_debugger default to self.debug, threaded defaults True. After showing the server banner it calls run_simple(host, port, self, **options); the finally block resets _got_first_request to False so the app can be restarted in an interactive shell. run_simple exceptions propagate after the finally runs.
units.summary: Run the development server via Werkzeug run_simple, resolving host/port/debug from config and env.

extras.note: May mutate self.debug and os environment via dotenv loading; resets _got_first_request in finally.
No-op with warning when FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI is 'true'.

units.explain: Returns a test client instance constructed as cls(self, self.response_class, use_cookies=use_cookies, **kwargs). cls is self.test_client_class; if that attribute is None it lazily imports flask.testing.FlaskClient. kwargs are forwarded to the client constructor, enabling custom client classes with extra parameters.
units.summary: Create a test client, defaulting to FlaskClient when test_client_class is unset.

units.explain: Returns a CLI test runner: cls is self.test_cli_runner_class, lazily importing flask.testing.FlaskCliRunner when None, then constructing cls(self, **kwargs) with the app as first argument and kwargs forwarded.
units.summary: Create a CLI test runner, defaulting to FlaskCliRunner when unset.

units.explain: Handles an HTTPException raised during dispatch. Exceptions with code None (proxy exceptions) are returned unchanged; RoutingException instances (internal routing signals like slash redirects) are returned without invoking error handlers. Otherwise it looks up a handler via _find_error_handler using the request's blueprints; if none is found the exception itself is returned (as the response value), otherwise the handler is run through ensure_sync with the exception and its return value returned.
units.summary: Route HTTPExceptions to error handlers, passing routing/proxy exceptions through unchanged.

units.explain: Handles an arbitrary exception raised during dispatch. A BadRequestKeyError in debug mode or when TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is set gets show_exception=True so the bad key is displayed. HTTPExceptions are forwarded to handle_http_exception unless trap_http_exception(e) says to trap them. For all other exceptions (or trapped HTTP ones), _find_error_handler looks up a handler by blueprints; if none exists the exception is re-raised bare (preserving the active traceback); otherwise the handler runs via ensure_sync and its value is returned.
units.summary: Dispatch exceptions to error handlers, re-raising when no handler matches.

units.explain: Last-resort handler for exceptions with no error handler or raised from a handler. Captures sys.exc_info(), sends got_request_exception (async-wrapped with ensure_sync), then evaluates PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS, defaulting to testing or debug when None. If propagating, re-raises bare when the passed exception is the active one (preserving traceback), else raises it. Otherwise logs via log_exception with the captured exc_info, builds InternalServerError(original_exception=e), and if a handler exists for it (found by blueprints) replaces server_error with the handler result. Finally returns finalize_request(ctx, server_error, from_error_handler=True), so after-request functions still run and failures in that path are logged rather than raised.
units.summary: Convert unhandled exceptions into a 500 InternalServerError response or re-raise when propagating.

extras.note: Sends the got_request_exception signal before any propagation decision.

units.explain: Logs the exception as an error on self.logger with the message "Exception on {request.path} [{request.method}]" and the given exc_info tuple. Reads the request path and method from the app context's request.
units.summary: Log the current request's exception via the app logger.

units.explain: Performs URL dispatch. If the request carries a routing_exception it is raised via raise_routing_exception. Otherwise the matched url_rule is taken; if automatic OPTIONS are provided for the rule and the method is OPTIONS, returns make_default_options_response. Otherwise the view function for rule.endpoint is looked up in view_functions, wrapped by ensure_sync (supporting async views), and called with the request's view_args; the raw return value is returned for later conversion by make_response.
units.summary: Match the rule and invoke the endpoint view, returning its raw value.

extras.note: raise_routing_exception may re-raise routing exceptions here; routing errors surface at this point.

units.explain: full_dispatch_request

Top of the per-request pipeline: on the first request, warns (DeprecationWarning, once per app via _got_first_request) that should_ignore_error is deprecated — but only when self.should_ignore_error is not None — then sets _got_first_request=True permanently. Sends request_started, runs preprocess_request, and if no before-request returned a value dispatches to dispatch_request. Any exception raised in that path is converted by handle_user_exception. The resulting value rv (response or error-handler output) is passed to finalize_request.
units.summary: Run preprocess and dispatch with error conversion, once per request.

extras.note: Sets _got_first_request True on the first request ever handled.

units.explain: Converts a view/exception-handler return value into a final Response: calls make_response, then process_response (after-request chain and session saving), then sends request_finished. If any of the postprocessing or signal raising raises, the exception propagates unless from_error_handler is True, in which case it is logged with logger.exception ('Request finalizing failed with an error while handling an error') and the response built so far is returned.
units.summary: Convert a return value to a Response, run after-request functions, and signal completion.

units.explain: Builds the automatic OPTIONS response: an empty response_class instance whose Allow header is updated with the allowed methods from the context's url_adapter. Override point for customizing OPTIONS behavior.
units.summary: Create the default OPTIONS response with the allowed-methods Allow header.

units.explain: Returns the function unchanged if it is a plain def; if iscoroutinefunction reports an async function it returns self.async_to_sync(func). Override point for customizing how async views are executed under WSGI.
units.summary: Return a sync-callable wrapper for async functions, pass others through.

units.explain: Wraps a coroutine function into a synchronous callable. Imports asgiref.sync.async_to_sync lazily; an ImportError becomes a RuntimeError instructing to install the 'async' extra, chained from None (hiding the import error). Returns the asgiref wrapper around func. Override point.
units.summary: Wrap an async function as sync via asgiref, erroring if asgiref is missing.

extras.note: RuntimeError when asgiref is not installed.

units.explain: Builds a URL for an endpoint. Inside an app context with a request, uses the context's url_adapter; an endpoint starting with '.' is resolved relative to the current blueprint (or the leading dot is stripped when not in a blueprint), and URLs are internal by default unless _scheme forces external. Outside a request, uses the app context's url_adapter if an app context is active, otherwise builds one from config; if no adapter can be created (no SERVER_NAME) raises RuntimeError. Outside a request URLs are external by default. Passing _scheme with _external=False raises ValueError (avoiding accidental insecure URLs). inject_url_defaults runs first; a BuildError from url_adapter.build is routed to handle_url_build_error with _anchor/_method/_scheme/_external merged into the values, whose string return becomes the result (otherwise BuildError propagates per the handler). A given _anchor is URL-quoted with a permissive safe set and appended as #anchor.
units.summary: Build a URL for an endpoint, resolving blueprints and defaulting externality by context.

extras.note: RuntimeError when building outside a request without SERVER_NAME; ValueError when _scheme is set with _external=False.

units.explain: Converts a view return value into a response_class instance. Tuple returns are unpacked: 3-tuples as (body, status, headers); 2-tuples are headers when the second element is Headers/dict/tuple/list, otherwise status; any other tuple length raises TypeError. None (including a view without return) raises TypeError naming the endpoint. Non-response bodies: str/bytes/bytearray or an Iterator are wrapped in response_class with the pending status/headers (then cleared); dict/list are converted via self.json.response; a werkzeug BaseResponse or any callable (WSGI app) is coerced via response_class.force_type with the current request environ, and a TypeError there is re-raised as a descriptive TypeError preserving the original traceback. Any other type raises TypeError listing the accepted forms. Afterwards a tuple-provided status (string/bytes form via rv.status, else rv.status_code) and headers (rv.headers.update) are applied. Requires an active request for the BaseResponse/callable coercion path (request.environ).
units.summary: Convert any supported view return value into the app's Response class.

relations.basis: both are response-building helpers on Flask; json.response used for dict/list

extras.note: TypeError for None returns, bad tuple lengths, and unrecognized body types.

units.explain: Runs pre-dispatch hooks in blueprint specificity order: names is (None, *reversed(request.blueprints)). First all url_value_preprocessors for those names run with (request.endpoint, request.view_args) (their results are not captured). Then before_request_funcs run in the same order, each via ensure_sync; the first non-None return value short-circuits and is returned as the effective view result, stopping dispatch. Returns None when all hooks pass.
units.summary: Run URL value preprocessors and before_request handlers, honoring first non-None result.

extras.note: A non-None before_request return replaces the view call entirely.

units.explain: Runs post-dispatch hooks and saves the session. First ctx._after_request_functions run (non-app/blueprint scoped), then after_request_funcs for the request's blueprints in order and app-level (None) in reversed registration order, each via ensure_sync, threading the response through. If the context's session is not a null session, session_interface.save_session(self, session, response) persists it onto the response. Returns the (possibly replaced) response, which must remain a response_class instance.
units.summary: Run after_request functions and save the session onto the response.

units.explain: Runs request teardown after the response is finalized, called from AppContext.pop. Uses a _CollectErrors accumulator so every callback runs even if earlier ones fail (3.2 behavior). Iterates chain(ctx.request.blueprints, (None,)) — blueprint-scoped first, app-level reversed — calling each teardown_request func with exc via ensure_sync inside the collector; then sends request_tearing_down under the collector. Finally raises a grouped error listing all failures via collect_errors.raise_any('Errors during request teardown').
units.summary: Run all request teardown functions and signal, collecting rather than short-circuiting errors.
uncertainties: raise_any raises only when errors were collected; exact exception type defined in flask/helpers.py

units.explain: Runs app-context teardown before the app context pops, called from AppContext.pop. Calls every teardown_appcontext func in reversed registration order with exc via ensure_sync inside a _CollectErrors accumulator, then sends appcontext_tearing_down under the collector, then raises collected errors via raise_any('Errors during app teardown') so all callbacks run despite failures.
units.summary: Run appcontext teardown functions and signal, collecting all errors before raising.

units.explain: Returns a new AppContext(self). Pushing it makes current_app and g available; contexts are pushed automatically per request and for flask CLI commands. No state is mutated here; pushing/popping is the context's own behavior.
units.summary: Create a new AppContext bound to this app.

units.explain: Returns AppContext.from_environ(self, environ), an app context carrying a request built from the WSGI environment. Intended for internal use; the docstring directs user code to test_request_context since constructing valid WSGI environs manually is error-prone.
units.summary: Create an AppContext with a request from a WSGI environ.

units.explain: Builds a request-bound AppContext for tests. Constructs an EnvironBuilder(self, *args, **kwargs) (Werkzeug EnvironBuilder arguments with Flask defaults from PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME, SERVER_NAME, APPLICATION_ROOT, etc.), calls builder.get_environ() with builder.close() in a finally so the builder is always cleaned up even if environ creation fails, then returns request_context(environ). Pushing the result provides request/session/g/current_app proxies.
units.summary: Create a test request context from EnvironBuilder arguments.

units.explain: The actual WSGI application, kept separate from __call__ so middleware can wrap it without losing the app object. Creates the request-bound context, pushes it, and runs full_dispatch_request. Any Exception during push/dispatch is stored as error and converted via handle_exception into a 500 response; a bare except re-captures the current exception as error and re-raises (propagating non-Exception BaseExceptions). The response is then invoked as response(environ, start_response) (the JSONProvider.response candidate in the graph refers to how dict returns become responses earlier; here response is already a Response/WSGI callable). The finally block always runs: if werkzeug.debug.preserve_context is in the environ the context is handed to the debugger, and should_ignore_error (if defined, deprecated) can clear the error before ctx.pop(error) so teardown sees None for ignorable errors.
units.summary: WSGI entry: push context, dispatch, convert errors, and always pop with the captured error.
uncertainties: The graph flags two candidates for response(environ, start_response); the listing shows response coming from full_dispatch_request/handle_exception, both Response objects, so the exact callee is not resolved here

extras.note: should_ignore_error, when defined, may downgrade the error passed to ctx.pop to None.

units.explain: WSGI-server entry point; simply delegates to wsgi_app(environ, start_response) so middleware should replace app.wsgi_app rather than wrapping the app object itself.
units.summary: Delegate the WSGI call to wsgi_app.

units.explain: Module header region: __future__ annotations import, stdlib and Werkzeug imports, intra-package imports (cli, typing, ctx, globals, helpers, sansio.app, sessions, signals, templating, wrappers), TYPE_CHECKING-only type imports, and module-level TypeVar declarations (T_shell_context_processor, T_teardown, T_template_filter, T_template_global, T_template_test) used as bounds for decorator typing. No executable behavior beyond imports and TypeVar creation.
units.summary: Imports and decorator TypeVar declarations for the Flask app module.
uncertainties: Signal and helper semantics live in their own modules

flask/app.py::module_residual::::0.reason: imports and TypeVars; documented as module header region

flask/app.py::module_residual::::2622.reason: TypeVar F declaration between decorator helpers; no behavior

flask/app.py::function::remove_ctx::2802.reason: continuation region of remove_ctx covered by the group

flask/app.py::function::add_ctx::3205::s.reason: continuation region of add_ctx covered by the group

flask/app.py::class::Flask::3592::s0.reason: class-level state and docstring; methods have own units

flask/app.py::method::Flask.create_url_a.reason: branching bind logic for host/subdomain matching

flask/app.py::method::Flask.log_exceptio.reason: error logging with request context formatting

flask/app.py::method::Flask.dispatch_req.reason: core dispatch with OPTIONS and view call

flask/app.py::method::Flask.finalize_req.reason: response finalization with error-handler safe mode

flask/app.py::method::Flask.url_for::439.reason: URL building with many branches and error handling

flask/app.py::method::Flask.make_respons.reason: large type-conversion logic with failure modes

flask/app.py::method::Flask.wsgi_app::63.reason: core WSGI pipeline with error capture

payload.batch_notes: Fixed the prior schema_error by adding the missing disposition for flask/app.py::module_residual::::3089, which is explained within the Flask class unit (it falls inside the class body holding default_config and class attributes). One placeholder unit (full_dispatch_request) is superseded by its proper unit; only the properly id'd unit is referenced in dispositions. Uncertainties recorded: raise_routing_exception with a None routing_exception, add_ctx without an active app context, add_ctx stacking on the Flask base class, and the exact callee of response(environ, start_response) in wsgi_app.
